s1.syndrome_frame: Enlarging, painful, purplish mass in the ear canal with granulomatous inflammation and atypical cells
salient_findings: Purplish-red mass in the left external ear canal
Irregular, friable surface with bleeding on minimal contact
Lobulated mass extending into the external acoustic canal and parotid space
Bilateral cervical lymph nodes up to 0.6 cm in diameter
Marked vascularity of the mass
key_facts: Purplish lump in the left ear canal
Cracking and pus-filled sores at the site
Contrast-enhanced CT showed a lobulated mass
Incisional biopsy revealed atypical cells and granulomatous inflammation

shortlist.label: Rhabdomyosarcoma
shortlist.why_kept: Aggressive tumor with rapid growth, common in children, and can present with a painful mass

shortlist.label: Langerhans cell histiocytosis
shortlist.why_kept: Can cause granulomatous inflammation and atypical cells, with possible involvement of the ear canal

shortlist.label: Angiosarcoma
shortlist.why_kept: Marked vascularity on CT angiography and rapid growth are consistent with this highly vascular tumor

shortlist.label: Merkel cell carcinoma
shortlist.why_kept: Can present with a rapidly growing, painful mass and has a high propensity for local invasion

shortlist.label: Granulomatous lymphoma
shortlist.why_kept: Presence of granulomatous inflammation and atypical cells on biopsy, with possible lymph node involvement

raw.rationale: The presence of a rapidly enlarging, painful mass with atypical cells and granulomatous inflammation, along with marked vascularity, is consistent with Rhabdomyosarcoma, a common malignant tumor in children that can occur in various sites, including the head and neck region.

rejected.label: Langerhans cell histiocytosis
rejected.why: Typically presents with multiple lesions and systemic symptoms, which are not mentioned in the vignette.

rejected.label: Angiosarcoma
rejected.why: More common in adults and typically presents with cutaneous lesions, which is not the primary presentation in this case.

rejected.label: Merkel cell carcinoma
rejected.why: Rarely occurs in children and typically presents as a solitary, painless nodule, which does not match the description of the mass in this case.

rejected.label: Granulomatous lymphoma
rejected.why: Not a well-established diagnosis, and the presence of atypical cells and marked vascularity is more suggestive of a sarcoma.
